documents.title: Responsible Use of AI at URI
documents.summary: An ITS page that welcomes AI for teaching, learning and research and sets four principles (transparency, accountability, fairness, privacy) plus data-security, accessibility and IP standards. It sets no default for coursework AI use: educators communicate acceptable use and students follow each instructor's policy and attribute AI content.
documents.stance_why: The page "embraces" AI but sets no rule on what is allowed in coursework; it tells educators to "clearly communicate acceptable AI use to students" and students to "Follow instructors’ AI policies", so the decision is handed to instructors (delegates).

units.why: "embraces artificial intelligence (AI) as a powerful tool for teaching, learning, research, and innovation" states a welcoming institutional position, so actor all, phase general, modality informs, encourage. P02 (permit or encourage by default) is where a reader asking whether URI welcomes AI would look; P56 fits less because the sentence states a position, not a framework.
units.resolution_why: Coder A chose P56 (framework preamble), coder B chose P02 (encourage by default); actor, phase, modality agreed. The source sentence is a headline position that AI is embraced, which is a stance on AI use; the framework content follows in later units. P02 chosen, with a fit_note because it is not a coursework default.
units.anchor: embraces artificial intelligence (AI) as a powerful tool for teaching, learning, research, and innovation
units.frag_start: The University of Rhode Island (URI) embraces
units.fit_note: Institution-wide welcome of AI for teaching, learning, research and innovation; it is not a coursework default (the page delegates that to instructors).

units.why: "ensuring AI is used securely, ethically, and responsibly" states the purpose and values of the page ("transparency, fairness, and accountability"), so an institution-wide framework (P56), informs. P116 is a close alternative but this sentence names the framework's values.
units.resolution_why: Both coders agreed on all codes (P56, general, informs, neutral). Only topic tags differed; kept the corpus topic vocabulary (B's ethics-bias-environment) plus governance from A. Anchor taken from B, a tighter quote.
units.anchor: ensuring AI is used securely, ethically, and responsibly

units.why: "Clearly disclose when AI tools are used to create content or make decisions" is the Transparency principle, a disclosure rule for all users; P24. It sits under "Guiding Principles", framed as values the approach is "built on", so should rather than must. Unit stance permit: AI use is allowed on condition of disclosure.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on actor, phase, P24. Modality: A must, B should. The sentence is in the Guiding Principles list (not the "URI enforces the following standards" list), so should. Unit stance: A permit, B require; "require" would mean AI use itself is required, which the text does not say; disclosure is a condition on permitted use, so permit.
units.anchor: Clearly disclose when AI tools are used to create content or make decisions

units.why: "Validate the accuracy of AI outputs" is the first clause of the Accountability principle, a verification duty; P31. The second clause (take responsibility) is coded separately as P29. Should, as a principle.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P31, general, all. A coded one unit for the whole sentence (must), B split the sentence into two units. The two clauses are two distinct rules, so split as B did. Modality should as the item is in the Guiding Principles list. Unit stance neutral (B said require, which is not supported).
units.anchor: Validate the accuracy of AI outputs
units.policy: Validate the accuracy of AI outputs
units.fit_note: Coder A noted the sentence also says users take responsibility for the use of outputs (ownership); that clause is coded as its own unit.

units.why: "take responsibility for their use" is the second clause of the Accountability principle, making users answerable for how they use AI outputs; closest to P29 (own what is submitted), although the text is not limited to submitted work.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B found this as a separate unit (A folded it into a fit_note on the P31 unit). The source sentence states two rules joined by 'and', so the second was kept as its own unit. P29 with a fit_note; modality should as for the other principles; unit stance neutral (B's require not supported).
units.anchor: take responsibility for their use
units.policy: Users take responsibility for their use of AI outputs
units.fit_note: Applies to all users' use of AI outputs, not only to submitted student work.

units.why: "Mitigate biases and ensure AI systems respect diversity and equity" is the Fairness and Inclusivity principle naming bias; P53. A Guiding Principle, so should.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P53, general, all, neutral; only modality differed (A must, B should). Item is in the Guiding Principles list, so should.
units.anchor: Mitigate biases and ensure AI systems respect diversity and equity

units.why: "Protect sensitive and institutional data from misuse and unauthorized access" is the Privacy and Security principle; P50. A Guiding Principle, so should.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P50, general, all, neutral; only modality differed (A must, B should). Item is in the Guiding Principles list, so should.
units.anchor: Protect sensitive and institutional data from misuse and unauthorized access

units.why: "URI Data Classification Schema and Guidelines" is listed under Key Resources with a description of what it covers, a pointer to further guidance; P115, informs.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded this resource link separately (B merged both Key Resources into one unit). It is a real pointer to guidance named by the institution, so kept; policy normalized from the page's own description.
units.anchor: URI Data Classification Schema and Guidelines
units.policy: The URI Data Classification Schema and Guidelines detail the classification and management of data, including restricted and sensitive information, relevant to AI practices.

units.why: "Guidelines for the Secure and Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence" is listed under Key Resources with a description of its coverage, a pointer to further guidance; P115, informs.
units.resolution_why: Both coders coded this resource as P115, general, informs, neutral. A anchored only the title, B anchored the description and wrote a normalized policy; B's wording is faithful to the source and kept. Topics: policy-evolution replaced by governance.
units.anchor: comprehensive guidance on AI transparency, accountability, and compliance with accessibility, privacy
units.frag_start: Guidelines for the Secure and Ethical
units.policy: Guidelines for the Secure and Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence provide guidance on AI transparency, accountability, and compliance with accessibility, privacy, and intellectual property standards

units.why: "Follow URI’s Data Classification Guidelines to avoid exposing restricted or sensitive information" is the Data Security and Privacy standard, an enforced standard binding all users; P50, must.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P50, general, all, must. Unit stance: A neutral, B restrict. The standard requires following data guidelines; it does not ban AI use, so neutral.
units.anchor: to avoid exposing restricted or sensitive information.
units.policy: Follow URI’s Data Classification Guidelines to avoid exposing restricted or sensitive information

units.why: "Ensure all AI tools comply with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)" is an enforced standard on accessibility of AI tools; P97, must.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on every code (P97, general, must, neutral). Only topic tags differed; kept the corpus topic equity-access.
units.anchor: Ensure all AI tools comply with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG)
units.policy: Ensure all AI tools comply with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)

units.why: "Avoid inputting private or restricted data, such as Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or patient records, into public AI tools like ChatGPT" is the Prohibited Data Use standard, a ban on one kind of input, so must-not. P50 (protect personal data) fits it; AI use itself stays allowed, so unit stance restrict.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P50, general, all, must-not. Unit stance: A restrict, B prohibit. The ban covers only one kind of data in public tools and AI use otherwise continues, so restrict. B's fit_note kept.
units.anchor: Avoid inputting private or restricted data
units.frag_end: into public AI tools like ChatGPT.
units.policy: Avoid inputting private or restricted data, such as Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or patient records, into public AI tools like ChatGPT
units.fit_note: Bans entering PII or restricted data into public AI tools; P50 is about protecting data and preferring vetted tools, not specifically about a prohibition.

units.why: "Be cautious when using AI platforms, as data entered may be transmitted to third-party servers" is the Data Handling Awareness standard, a caution about data privacy; P50, should because "be cautious" is advisory.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on every code (P50, general, all, should, neutral).
units.anchor: data entered may be transmitted to third-party servers

units.why: "Where possible, disable history and logging features to prevent information from being stored or used for AI training without consent" is the Disabling Data Logging standard, a hedged privacy practice; P50, should because of "Where possible".
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on every code (P50, general, all, should, neutral). B's wording of the policy is faithful to the source and kept.
units.anchor: disable history and logging features to prevent information from being stored
units.policy: Where possible, disable history and logging features to prevent information from being stored or used for AI training without consent

units.why: "Respect copyrights and avoid using confidential data in AI systems without appropriate protections in place" is the Intellectual Property Compliance standard, an enforced standard; P52 chosen for the copyright clause, must.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P52, general, all, must. Unit stance: A neutral, B restrict. The data clause is conditional on protections and AI is not otherwise limited, so neutral. Both coders' fit_notes (the same point) kept as one.
units.anchor: Respect copyrights and avoid using confidential data in AI systems
units.policy: Respect copyrights and avoid using confidential data in AI systems without appropriate protections in place
units.fit_note: Also says to avoid confidential data in AI systems without protections, which is a privacy rule (P50).

units.why: "Attend sessions on responsible AI use tailored for faculty, staff, and students" encourages training participation under Education and Training; P70. An imperative inside a list of opportunities, so should.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P70, general, all, encourage. Modality: A should, B may. The text uses the imperative "Attend", so should.
units.anchor: Attend sessions on responsible AI use tailored for faculty, staff, and students

units.why: "Access documents and guidelines like the AI Use Guidelines to deepen understanding" points users to training materials under Education and Training; P70, should for the same imperative form as the neighbouring item.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded this item (A: may). It is a real statement under Education and Training and distinct from the workshops item, so kept; modality set to should to match the imperative form used for "Attend sessions".
units.anchor: Access documents and guidelines like the

units.why: "Learn how to make AI tools and outputs more inclusive" under Accessibility Resources is a learning duty about accessible AI; P97 rather than P70 because its content is accessibility. Should (imperative, advisory training).
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P97, general, all, should. Unit stance: A encourage, B neutral; it is about inclusivity rather than AI use itself, so neutral.
units.anchor: Learn how to make AI tools and outputs more inclusive
units.policy: Learn how to make AI tools and outputs more inclusive through URI’s accessibility programs

units.why: "Before using any AI platform, take the time to understand how it works, what data it collects, and how it handles that data" asks users to evaluate a tool before use; P117, should.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on every code (P117, general, all, should, neutral).
units.anchor: Before using any AI platform, take the time to understand how it works
units.policy: Before using any AI platform, users take the time to understand how it works, what data it collects, and how it handles that data

units.why: "Incorporate URI’s guidelines into course design" tells educators to build the university's AI guidelines into how they design courses; P77 (comply with existing university policy), with a fit_note because the rule is specifically about course design. Phase before-course; should, as an Additional Guideline.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: UNCOVERED, should; coder B: P77, should. Actor, phase agreed. The "AI Use Guidelines" are university policy and the rule is to comply with them in course design, so P77 fits; the design-specific point is kept in a fit_note (A's uncovered_note merged).
units.anchor: Incorporate URI’s guidelines into course design
units.policy: Educators incorporate URI’s guidelines into course design
units.fit_note: Specifically concerns aligning course design with the university's AI guidelines (coder A had coded this UNCOVERED: educators should build the university AI guidelines into their course design).

units.why: "clearly communicate acceptable AI use to students" makes educators state their AI expectations; P09 (AI statement) with a fit_note because the syllabus is not mentioned. Instructor, course-start, should.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on every code (P09, instructor, course-start, should, neutral) and both wrote the same fit_note; kept once.
units.anchor: clearly communicate acceptable AI use to students
units.policy: Educators clearly communicate acceptable AI use to students
units.fit_note: Says to communicate acceptable use to students but not specifically in the syllabus.

units.why: "disclose when AI was used to create course materials" is instructor disclosure of AI-made materials; P48 (review and disclose AI-made materials), before-course, should as an Additional Guideline.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P48, instructor, before-course. Modality: A must, B should; the item is in Additional Guidelines worded as role guidance, so should. Unit stance: A neutral, B require; neutral, as the text does not require AI use.
units.anchor: disclose when AI was used to create course materials
units.policy: Educators disclose when AI was used to create course materials
units.fit_note: Disclosure is stated; review of materials is not mentioned.

units.why: "Follow instructors’ AI policies" makes each instructor's policy the rule students follow; P78, student, general, should as an Additional Guideline.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P78, student, general, neutral. Modality: A must, B should; Additional Guidelines are role guidance, so should. A's anchor "Follow instructors" was too short; B's anchor used.
units.anchor: Follow instructors’ AI policies

units.why: "properly attribute AI-generated content" asks students to attribute AI output; P24, during-work, should as an Additional Guideline. Unit stance permit: use is allowed on condition of attribution.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P24, student, during-work. Modality: A must, B should; chose should as for the other Additional Guidelines. Unit stance: A permit, B require; permit, because attribution is a condition and AI use is not required.
units.anchor: properly attribute AI-generated content

units.why: "avoid using AI in ways that breach URI’s Student Code of Conduct" ties AI use to existing conduct rules; P77, should-not, restrict. P36 fits less because it does not classify misuse as misconduct or name a process.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P77, student, general, restrict. Modality: A must-not, B should-not; Additional Guidelines are role guidance, so should-not.
units.anchor: avoid using AI in ways that breach URI’s Student Code of Conduct
units.policy: Students avoid using AI in ways that breach URI’s Student Code of Conduct

units.why: "Consult with your department and comply with regulations when using AI tools in research" sets research AI duties and defers to department and regulations; P62. The Researchers guideline has no actor value of its own, so actor all; should as an Additional Guideline.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P62, general, all, neutral. Modality: A must, B should; Additional Guidelines, so should. A's fuller anchor kept, with B's normalized policy.
units.anchor: Consult with your department and comply with regulations when using AI tools in research
units.policy: Researchers consult with their department and comply with regulations when using AI tools in research, particularly for handling sensitive or proprietary data

units.why: "For more information about URI’s AI practices and resources, contact: karen_lokey@uri.edu" points to a contact for further information; P115, informs.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded the closing contact line. It is a pointer to further AI information, so kept. A's anchor was only the email address; replaced with the full sentence. A's fit_note kept.
units.anchor: For more information about URI’s AI practices and resources, contact: karen_lokey@uri.edu
units.fit_note: Names a contact person for information, not an owner of the policy.

notes: Only uri-responsible-ai was coded; uri-grad-ai (a thin Graduate School news post) was screened out in the collect file. Imperatives in the Guiding Principles and Additional Guidelines were coded should/should-not; imperatives in the 'URI enforces the following standards' list were coded must/must-not. B's corpus-standard topic tags were used.
